name: Sunglow
lede: Sunglow is a bright, golden yellow named for the glow of the sun, and a name found in color charts more than in older books.

sections.title: The pink or yellow glow of the sun
sections.body:
In Paterson's dictionary, sun-glow names the light of a sunrise or an afterglow, which may be pink or yellowish [1]. He lists it among the yellows near *sunflower* and *sun yellow* [2][3]. The books record no date and no pigment, and nothing ties the name to a specific maker [1].

The swatch here is a saturated golden yellow; Paterson points his sun yellow entry to [[maize]] [3]. In Paterson's own sense the word could just as well mean a pink dawn, a reminder that a name can outlast its color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 18 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed [4]. The earliest sample is a portrait of Ivan Vadbolsky from 1823 [4]. The match counts any painting with this color covering at least a twentieth of the canvas, so it shows where the color appears in photographs of paintings, not that the painters ever called it by this name.
